Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779

 

Published December 10, 2025

 

Summary

 

Open a business trust, business pension or profit-sharing plan trust, estate-nonindividual personal representative, receivership-individual receiver, Girl Scout council or Girl Scout Troop DBA, government entity, or Indian tribal government entity account.

 

Select the section heading to expand the procedure content.

 

Business trust, business pension or profit-sharing plan trust

 

Understand the rules 

  •       The Customer Identification Program (CIP) requirement is designed to enable the bank to form a reasonable belief about an individual’s and nonindividual’s true identity for all new and existing deposit accounts, loans, financial products, contracts, safe deposit boxes, or any other type of banking service or product.
    •      The process of forming a reasonable belief is taking steps to verify the identity, credentials, identification, and other supporting information provided by potential and existing customers.
    •      You must provide the required disclosures, notices, and information to potential and existing customers.
  •       The Customer Due Diligence (CDD) requirement enables Cayman Bank to know its customers and understand the nature and purpose of accounts and relationships to develop a customer risk profile.
  •       Refer to the CSBB 1FC Program Document for additional details on Sanctions situations, UAR submission, CIP requirements, CDD requirements, and Beneficial Ownership requirements.
  •       Compare the provided customer information to the customer identification (ID) or proof-of-entity documentation.
  •       A completed Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers form must be obtained, certified, and signed by the customer at new account opening or business customer relationship maintenance to be valid and acceptable
    Reference: CIP and CDD Resources
  •       When opening a business deposit account, at least one owner or key executive with entity authority and control must have a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) (for example, SSN or ITIN). If they do not, the business account cannot be opened.
  •       A customer request to open a new deposit account must not be declined for the:
    •      Account may be open only a short time
    •      Customer has or will have duplicate accounts
  •       Employees may open business deposit accounts for customers meeting the following criteria:
    •      Are nonindividual entity customers (including sole proprietorships, business trusts, business pension or profit-sharing trust, corporations, limited liability companies, limited liability partnerships, joint venture, general partnerships, social and recreational clubs, unincorporated associations, and civic groups).
    •      Have gross annual sales of less than $2 million.
    •      Do not require Treasury Management Services.
    •      Do not have complex lending needs.

If the business does not meet the criteria, the employee must refer the customer to the appropriate partner or affiliate.

Related procedure: Referrals to Partners or Affiliates

  •       Disclosures: If disclosures are not available, the account cannot be opened. A supply of disclosure New Account Kits (NAKs) may be obtained from another location. If the customer wants to receive the disclosure electronically and has access to their email through their mobile device, the account can be opened.
  •       Employees must not sign or otherwise place a customer’s signature on a document on the customer’s behalf or in lieu of the customer physically signing. Print or digital copies of signatures obtained from the customer on previous documents must not be used when a signature is required on a new document.
  •       Employees are prohibited from entering into any customer provided agreements, up to and including agreements barring Branch Banking from sharing due diligence information with Financial Crimes Risk Management (FCRM), Internal Audit, regulators, or other similar functions. Any existing accounts with external agreements identified after account opening will be immediately exited.
  •       When opening a new account for a business, the individuals who provide personal financial information in connection with the business must be given the opportunity to elect whether to share personal information with other Cayman Bank affiliates.
  •       Treasury Management deposit products are restricted from being offered to customers (for example, Controlled Disbursement, Stagecoach deposit). Only business account products can be opened by branch employees.
    •      Refer to the Products database for currently available accounts.
    •      Referrals must be directed to the appropriate partner or affiliate.
      Related procedure: Referrals to Partners or Affiliates
  •       Employees must not travel outside of the U.S. for purposes of conducting bank business or discussing bank related products or services.
  •       A new account request must be blocked or restricted if the transaction is conducted by, for, or on behalf of countries, entities, or individuals affected by the Foreign Assets Control regulations.
  •       When the tax-responsible customer (for example, business account owner, third party, client, or insolvent party) is an entity, trust, or estate formed in a U.S. territory, a noninterest-earning product must be used.
  •       Prohibited high-risk industries are not permitted to open or maintain deposit accounts or Safe Deposit Box Relationships.
  •       Deposit accounts and Safe Deposit Box Relationships for restricted high-risk industries can be opened after they have been reviewed and approved by Enhanced Due Diligence Center (EDDC).
  •       Certain unregulated or unlicensed financial institutions are prohibited from being opened or maintained. These industries must be reviewed and approved by Enhanced Due Diligence Center (EDDC) prior to opening the account.
  •       If a due diligence review is required, and the customer indicates either of the following, a Suspected Risk Referral (SRR) must be submitted, and a new account request must be denied:
    •      Refuses to provide information required to complete due diligence.
    •      Suspiciously indicates they provided the wrong responses to the compliance questions after the banker already disclosed the enhanced diligence requirements to the customer.
  •       Multiple signature requirements are not allowed on a deposit account.
  •       A fee waiver must not be placed on an account only because the customer has objected to the standard fees.
  •       A Pay on Death (POD) beneficiary may only be added to an account if the business entity is a sole proprietorship and is not an IOLTA, RETA, or public fund account. Other types of business entities (for example, corporations, partnerships, or limited liability companies) are ineligible for a POD beneficiary.
  •       First deposit for new account: The minimum deposit requirement must be met and made at the time of the account opening.

Exception: When a court- or government-appointed fiduciary indicates funds are not available to be deposited to the new account but will be deposited in the future, a minimum deposit is not required. Tell the customer the account must be funded within 30 calendar days, or it may be subject to closure.

Examples of court- or government-appointed fiduciary account types are:

  •      Lottery
  •      Attorney client trust
  •      Business trust
  •      Estate – Nonindividual personal representative
  •      Real-estate trust
  •      Representative payee
  •      Individual and nonindividual guardian or conservator
  •      Individual and nonindividual receiverships
  •      Statutory client trust

Note: The minimum deposit amount is always required for a time deposit account.

  •       Before opening a deposit account, risk screening must be completed on the following individuals:
    •      Owners with 25% or more ownership that have entity authority and control
    •      Key executives with entity authority and control

Note: Owners with less than 25% entity ownership with authority and control added to the business relationship will also be risk screened but it is not required.

Exception: Risk screening is not required for the following individuals:

  •      Nonindividual owners with or without entity authority and control
  •      Individual owners without entity authority and control
  •      Key executives of a U.S. government unit or agency, or Indian tribal government
  •      For benefit of (FBO) accounts for a title company with an approved Title Escrow Service Agreement on file
  •      Trustee who owns 25% or more of an entity, and authorized signers who are not owners (with entity authority and control)
  •       Tell the customer when additional time or assistance is required to review the transaction.
  •       Transaction approvers: Introduce yourself to the customer and explain your role when you are asked to review a transaction or request.

References:

  •      Transaction approval guide
  •      Branch Banking de-escalation guide
  •       Publicly traded, non-publicly traded, profit or nonprofit entity status change requires the following:
    •      Closing the existing and opening a new account
    •      Creating a new entity customer record
    •      Completing a new Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers form

For additional information, refer to the Create or Maintain an Individual Record or Entity Record procedure.

  •       Business Pension or Profit-sharing plan trust: A business pension or profit-sharing plan trust (for example, a pension plan, profit-sharing or 401(k) plan) has two components: the plan and the trust.
    •      The plan describes the benefits and IRS requirements. A plan administrator is appointed to make decisions for the plan. The plan is legally separate from the trust.

Note: People who are unfamiliar with retirement funds tend to use the words plan and trust interchangeably.

  •      The trust holds the plan funds. The trust has a trustee who is the individual with control over the trust and conducts transactions for the trust based on direction from the plan administrator. Accounts are opened in the name of the trust.

Note: The name of the plan may be the same as or different from the name of the trust.

  •       Escalate the following based on the situation:

Situation

Action

A nexus (connection) to a sanctioned country
Examples:

  •           Citizenship
  •           Permanent residency
  •           Address

Refer to the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Requirements procedure to properly escalate.

An individual with a nexus (connection) to Cuba, Iran, or North Korea

Before opening or maintaining relationships for an account, follow the requirements in the Onboard a customer or other associated party with a nexus to a sanctioned country section in the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Requirements procedure.

  •       All sanctions-related actions should only be performed as directed by FC Risk Management and the Global Sanctions Screening and Reporting Group (GSSRG) team.

The following not all-inclusive list is examples of how to identify a nexus (connection) to Cuba, Iran, or North Korea:

  •      Self-Identify: Conversing with the individual and they provide that information (for example, while completing a transaction request, answering country of citizenship or address questions)
  •      Document Review: Reviewing identification or other documentation the customer provides (for example, Iran Passport, U.S. Passport stating the place of birth is Cuba, proof of address)
  •       If you identify any red flags or unusual activity, submit an SRR.

 

Certification of Trustee
Do not complete a Certification of Trustee form.

Backup withholding and exemptions
Refer to the Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and Foreign Status Maintenance, Certification, and Backup Withholding procedure.

Open an account to hold third-party funds in a specially designated trust relationship account

Some business industries are required to hold third-party funds in specially designated trust relationship accounts. The following relationships are not business trusts.
Complete the Business Deposit Account: Fiduciary Relationships procedure for the following:

  •           Attorney–client trust (one-named client)
  •           Attorney-client trust (commingled or pooled funds)
  •           Interest on Lawyer's Trust Account (IOLTA)
  •           Real estate trust account (one-named client)
  •           Real estate trust - RETA account (commingled or pooled funds)

Note: If Cayman Bank does not offer the RETA account in the state, no special product is required. Open the account in the name of the entity. All account-opening requirements are based on the type of entity requesting the account (for example, corporation, sole proprietor, partnership, joint venture.

  •           Coogan trust or child entertainer trust (one-named child):Open Consumer Deposit Accounts

This procedure is complete.

Open a fiduciary relationship that is not a business trust or business pension or profit-sharing plan trust

A business trust is a legal entity set up for the control and management of assets and property. Trustees manage and control the assets for the business trust’s beneficiaries. The following relationships are not business trusts or business pension or profit-sharing plan trust. Complete the applicable procedures:

  •           Nonindividual Conservator, Nonindividual guardian or Nonindividual representative payee: Business Deposit Account: Fiduciary Relationships
  •           Revocable or irrevocable personal trust with individual or nonindividual trustees:Open Consumer Deposit Accounts
  •           Estate:Estate (nonindividual personal representative) and receivership (individual receiver) section

This procedure is complete.

Discuss products and services

  1.       Complete the Discover Needs Tool - CRV procedure to select the best product based on customer’s needs. Then return to this procedure and complete the remaining steps.
  2.       Review all product-related information with the customer, including the following information, for each product:
    •       Minimum opening deposit amount
    •       Monthly service fee amount and options to avoid the fee during the fee period
    •       Time accounts: Sufficient information to understand the Regulation D early withdrawal penalty, bank early withdrawal fees, and when they apply
    •       Interest-bearing accounts:  When verbally discussing rates for deposit products or responding to a customer inquiry while face-to-face (in-person) with a customer, you must provide the correct numerical value of the Annual Percentage Yield (APY) and use the correct full term (Annual Percentage Yield) or acronym (APY). During this discussion, the standard, relationship, or special interest rate may be stated in addition to the Annual Percentage Yield (APY).

Example: You will receive an Annual Percentage Yield (APY) of 0.25% (example only and not actual Yield).

  1.       Provide the following funds options to the customer, if applicable, and ask how they will fund the account today with the minimum required amount:
    •       Deposit at a teller line
    •       Cayman Bank ATM
    •       Cayman Bank Mobile® deposit, available in the Cayman Bank Mobile® app
    •       Transferring funds from another Cayman Bank account through Cayman Bank Online® at Cayman Bank.com or the Cayman Bank Mobile app
    •       Zelle® or another business to business or consumer to business payment method

Note: If the customer cannot fund the account today with the required minimum amount, tell them you cannot open the account. Offer to schedule an appointment for the customer to return at a later date to open and fund the account. This procedure is complete.
Exception: When a court- or government-appointed fiduciary indicates funds are not available to be deposited to the new account but will be deposited in the future, a minimum deposit is not required. Tell the customer the account must be funded within 30 calendar days, or it may be subject to closure.
The minimum deposit is required when the customer is opening a Business Trust Time Deposit Account.

The employee opening the account must be the one to identify the individuals and obtain required customer information.
Refer to the Business Deposit Account: Fiduciary relationships procedure.

One or more customers are present

Verify customer information

 

  1. Verify the entity existence using the Business Deposit Account: Entity Verification procedure.

Note: There is no requirement to send entity verification documentation to Business Document Review.

  1. Business trusts: If a business trust is a nonprofit, their status must be verified.
    1. Access the IRS website using the Tax Exempt Organization Search Tool to verify entity’s nonprofit status.

Exception: Churches (including integrated auxiliaries and conventions or associations of churches) that meet the requirements of section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code are automatically considered tax-exempt and may not have filed their nonprofit tax-exempt status with the IRS. Print, scan, and submit a copy of the church’s Secretary of State filing that confirms their 501(c)(3) nonprofit status.

  1. Search for the entity name.
  2. Print a copy of the Summary page and keep for scanning later in this procedure.

Notes:

  • For a filed entity that cannot be located on the IRS website, access and search the Secretary of State (SOS) website for the entity. If the entity is listed as a nonprofit entity, this can be used to verify the entity’s nonprofit status.
  • There is not a requirement that all nonprofits be filed as 501(C) (3). To be classified as a nonprofit the entity just must be filed with the Secretary of State website as a nonprofit.
  • Religious organizations (for example, churches, including their integrated auxiliaries, conventions or associations, and ministries) that meet the requirements of section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code are automatically considered tax-exempt and may not have filed their nonprofit tax-exempt status with the IRS. Access the Secretary of State (SOS) filing to confirm their 501(c)(3) nonprofit status.
  • If a religious organization’s nonprofit status cannot be verified through the SOS or IRS websites, request additional documentation evidence to confirm status (for example, a determination letter from the IRS, a certificate of incorporation [must state entity is a nonprofit], a statement from a state taxing body verifying nonprofit status).
  1. Complete the following:

Note: Refer to Nonprofit Entity Confirmation Guidelines for further guidance.

  • Nonprofit is verified: Go to step 3.
  • Nonprofit is not verified: Tell the customer you cannot open the account. This procedure is complete.
  1. If assistance is needed to determine if entity documentation is acceptable to open an account, complete the following steps:
    1. Prepare an email to Business Document Review and provide the following information:
      • Clearly stated questions
      • Customer information (for example, account number, enterprise customer number, entity name, owner name, key executive name)
    2. Scan, attach, and send all entity documentation to Business Document Review. They will respond by email within 48 hours.
    3. If inquiring on a previously submitted question, include the Customer Care Now (CCN) number.

Example: The ABC Company is requesting to open an account. The entity is a business trust but is providing meeting minutes as their entity verification documentation. Search was completed on the SOS website and the filing document cannot be located. Is the documentation provided an acceptable form of entity verification documentation to open the account?

  1. Access and complete a Google search to confirm the physical business address provided is correct, makes sense for the type of business, and supports the nature of the business to ensure fraud mitigation.

Note: To complete address verification to satisfy Customer Identification Program and Customer Due Diligence (CIP/CDD), refer to the Business Deposit Account: Entity Verification procedure.

  • Business physical address confirmed: Go to the Open the account section.

Examples on how to confirm the business address:

  • Search the physical business address on Google Maps to confirm the address does not belong to:
    • A vacant building
    • A different business
    • A mail drop location
    • A parcel of land without a building
    • An apartment or house when the type of business could not possibly be home-based
  • Search the business name, physical address, and phone number on SuperPages or YellowPages to validate they match the information provided by the customer.

Note: Recently opened businesses may not display on SuperPages or YellowPages.

  • Business physical address is not confirmed: Tell the customer the account cannot be opened because the physical business address is not confirmed. This procedure is complete.

 

Open the account

 

Complete these steps (as applicable) in the following order to open the account:

Step 1: Process court-blocked accounts

For court orders or other legal restrictions presented on the account:

  1. Obtain the original or certified copy of the court document for bank records and return the original to the individual.
  2. Call the Court Blocked Accounts department for further instructions at 1-866-990-1324 (internal use only), Monday through Friday, 6:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Pacific Time.

Note: The Court Blocked Accounts department will add a hard hold restraint to the account.

Step 2: Create or update the customer records

  1. Search, select, review, create, or update the customer record for the entity, individual, or nonindividual owners (includes trust owners), key executives or trustee for Trust customer records and add them to the customer list.
    Notes:
    • Select the Pencil icon in the Business Relationship section of the entity customer record and add the owners, key executives, or trustee for Trust owner to the entity business relationship.
    • When opening a business deposit account, at least one owner or key executive with entity authority and control must have a TIN (for example, SSN or ITIN). If they do not, the business account cannot be opened.
    • Trust owns 25% or more of the legal entity: Create or update the trust and one trustee’s customer record (individual or nonindividual).
  2. Ensure the following:
    • Individual: The individual’s name must match the legal name listed on their primary ID, including middle initials and suffixes if applicable (for example, Jr., Sr.). Correct the name as needed.

Note: If the individual being added as the new owner, key executive, or trustee is not present, ensure the required notarized forms have been completed and presented for processing. Complete the following when creating a customer record for an individual being added who is not present:

  1. Select Customer not present > Written as the request method.
  2. Create the new individual customer record.
  3. Select Create individual record to create the prospect customer record.
  4. Select the Identification Pencil icon.
  5. Select Customer present > Primary ID.
  6. Select Notarized document > Account Application.
  7. Type Notarized document in the Description Field.
  8. Select Authenticate.
  9. Continue to complete all other required fields for a full customer record.
  • Entity: The name and address must match the entity name and physical address listed on the entity verification documentation.

Note: For an entity with no annual gross sales, enter 0 (zero) in the Annual Gross Sales field.

  1. Document any entity or individual name discrepancy using the ID Discrepancy Resolution field.

Examples of name discrepancies are:

  • Entity’s full legal name does not fit in the two-line field and must be abbreviated:Add the full legal name (for example, The International Association of Electrical Engineering Professionals Association).
  • Owner or key executive name in the business documents does not match their full legal name (first, middle initial, last) in the individual customer record: Add the owner’s full legal name (for example, James John Smith, but he is also known as John Smith which is listed in the business document).

For additional information, refer to the CIP and CDD Error Prevention for Small Business Deposit Accounts - Using the ID Discrepancy Resolution field guide.

  1. Complete the Customer Privacy: Maintenance, Data Requests, and Contact Information Confidentiality procedure if the owner, key executive, or trustee participates in the state-sponsored Address Confidentiality Program.

Note: Complete the Customer Privacy: Maintenance, Data Requests, and Contact Information Confidentiality procedure if the owner or key executive operates their business out of their home, and they participate in ADCON. Add an explanation in the ID Discrepancy Resolution field to explain the address discrepancy (for example, owner is a participant in the Address Confidentiality Program).

  1. Select Streamline Business Sales.

  • For an entity with no annual gross sales, enter 0 (zero) in the Annual Gross Sales field.

Step 3: Complete compliance verification

  1. Read the Compliance Validation questions to the customer and record their response (Yes or No).
    1. After you entered responses on the system, verified the responses with the customer, and advanced to the next screen, do not:
      • Select Previous or browser Back button to go back and change original answers selected.
      • Close out of the SVP session and open a new session to select different answers to the compliance questions.

Exception: Bankers may only select Previous on the system and correct any compliance question responses for the following situations:

  • A banker error was made in documenting the customer’s responses.
  • The customer provided an incorrect response to one or more of the compliance questions.
  • The customer is considering or now/newly involved in Payment Intermediary or high-risk business activities.
  • The customer is no longer involved in Payment Intermediary or high-risk business activities.
  1. Select Continue.
  2. If there are any Yes responses, go to step 2.

If all responses to the compliance questions are No, go to step 3.

  1. Complete the following actions if there is a Yes response to any of the questions and messaging indicates Enhanced Due Diligence is required:
    1. Tell the customer:
      • An additional review and approval are required before the account can be opened.
      • The review and approval process may take up to 90 calendar days to complete.
      • Approved accounts used for Money Services Business (MSB) activity have a $75 non-negotiable monthly fee.
    2. Complete the appropriate actions based on whether the customer understands the additional review or approval requirements and wants to continue with the account open request:
      • Customer does not want to continue: Close out of your SVP session and complete an SRR. This procedure is complete.
      • Customer wants to continue: Obtain all required customer information and identification for each owner with 10% or more direct or indirect ownership of the entity.
    3. Search for, create, or update the owners or key executives’ individual customer record.

Note: The individual customer records of business owners or key executives with a foreign address must be created in Streamline Business Sales.

  1. Ensure the individual’s name on the customer record matches the legal name listed on their primary ID, including middle initials and suffixes if applicable (for example, Jr., Sr.).
  2. Search for, create, or update the Business Relationships for the entity.
    Note: Select the Pencil icon in the Business Relationship section of the entity customer record and add the owners, key executives, or trustee for Trust owner to the entity business relationship.
  3. Print and ask the customer to complete the Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers (10%) (596622) form for business trust that is a corporation.
    Notes:
    • Complete the required banker information in the Bank Use Only section on the Beneficial Owner form.
    • Confirm that all information on the beneficial owners form matches the information on the entity and individual customer records for the business and related parties.
    • When completing the manual beneficial owner form it must either be typed or handwritten but not a combination of both.
    • The Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers form must not contain any alterations, changes, or corrections. If there are any, a new form is required.
    • Do not:
      • Use your Banker Stamp (SRS22 or SRS22M) or any other stamp on the body of the Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers form.
      • Add or write any information on the Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers form including CIP/CDD clearing error instructions or comments outside of the Bank Use Only sections.
    • No form is required for a business trust or business pension or profit-sharing plan trust that is an unincorporated association social, recreational, or civic group.
  4. Contact the Enhanced Due Diligence Center (EDDC) by email and provide the following information:
    • Subject line: Add type of referral (for example, MSB referral, TPP referral, CBD referral, Crowdfunding referral, Donor Advise Funds referral, or Marketplace [online] Lending referral)
    • Entity’s legal name
    • Enterprise Customer Number (ECN)
    • TIN
    • Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers 10% form, and any other business filing or formation documents, or licensing documents obtained
    • high-risk type identified (for example, Internet Gambling, Third-Party Payment Processor, Money Service Business, Cannabis Related Business, Crowdfunding, Donor Advised Funds, Marketplace [online] Lending)
  5. Place documents in a secure branch file until a decision is made on the account, then securely destroy the documents.
  6. Tell the customer they will be notified by the EDDC regarding the final decision to open the business deposit account.

Note: The EDDC will communicate the case’s outcome to the banker and customer. Do not open accounts or products until the EDDC approves.

  1. Select Yes or No in the Owners with 25% or more ownership, trustees (key executives), or trustees for trust owner with 25% or more ownership listed are correct field.
    • Select Yes when all owners, trustees (key executives), or trustees for trust owner with 25% or more ownership have been added. Select Continue. Go to the Step 5: Certify Beneficial Owner of Legal Entity Customers section.
    • Select No if additional owners, trustees (key executives), or trustees for trust owner with 25% or more ownership need to be added and complete the required information. Go to step 7.
      • Create or update the individual customer record for each owner, key executive, or trustee (of the trust with 25% or more ownership) listed on the Business Owners and Key executive screen.

  2. Complete the Customer Privacy: Maintenance, Data Requests, and Contact Information Confidentiality procedure if the owners, key executives, or trustees for trust owner with 25% or more ownership participates in the state-sponsored Address Confidentiality Program.

Notes:

  • Complete the Customer Privacy: Maintenance, Data Requests, and Contact Information Confidentiality procedure if the owner or key executive is operating their business out of their home. Add an explanation in the ID Discrepancy Resolution field to explain the address discrepancy (for example, owner is a participant in the Address Confidentiality Program).
  • If you need to add more than seven individual and nonindividual owners, key executives, or trustee, add the nonindividual and individual owners with 25% or more ownership with entity authority and control first, the add key executives with entity authority and control. Add the remaining owners and key executives later in the procedure.
  • When a trust owns 25% or more of the entity customer, the trust name and trustee Beneficial Owner information will be included on the Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers form.
  • You may complete a limited customer record, with fewer required fields, if it displays for nonindividual owners with or without control.
  • Document any entity or individual name discrepancy using the ID Discrepancy Resolution field.

Examples of name discrepancies are:

  • Entity’s full legal name does not fit in the two-line field and must be abbreviated:Add the full legal name (for example, The International Association of Electrical Engineering Professionals Trust).
  • Owner or key executive name in the business documents does not match their full legal name (first, middle initial, last) in the individual customer record:Add the owner’s full legal name (for example, James John Smith, but he is also known as John Smith which is listed in the business document).

For additional information, refer to the CIP and CDD Error Prevention for Small Business Deposit Accounts - Using the ID Discrepancy Resolution field guide.

Step 5: Certify Beneficial Owner of Legal Entity Customers

  1. Select the owner or key executive who will sign the Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers form in the Individual Certifying Beneficial Ownership field on the Select Certification Signer screen.

Step 6: Complete risk screening

  1. Complete the Qualify Customers screen.
    1. If the individual being risk screened has not been at the current address for the last 5 years, select the states where they resided from the States of Residence Last 5 Years drop-down menu.
    2. Select the appropriate option in the Able to Sign Forms section and obtain signatures of individuals being risk screened or manager or designee attestation if individual is not capable of signing the forms.
    3. Select Continue.
    4. If individuals being risk screened is present, the Authorization for Information in Connection with a Business Account Application (BACC) (BBG18141) form will display. Print, review, and obtain the customer’s signatures using the PIN Pad.

If not, obtain a completed, signed, and notarized Authorization for Information in Connection With a Business Account Application (BACC) (BBG18141) form before risk screening is processed.

  1. The manual form must be scanned for signature verification before risk screening can be completed.
    1. Print the Scanner Cover Sheet if displayed.
    2. Scan the manually completed Authorization for Information in Connection With a Business Account Application (BACC) (BBG18141) form.

Note: If a manual form is presented, the individual’s signature must be verified as being captured on the form. If there are signature capture questions or issues, refer to the Obtaining Consent and Signatures procedure.

  • No risk screen results display in the Qualify Results field: Select Continue. Go to the Step 7: Add authorized signers section.

Note: Risk screen results may not display if the risk screen response times out. Proceed with the account opening and an approval/override reason will not be required. Day 2 risk screening will still occur.

  • Banker wants to open the account even though the customers is not approved: Overriding a negative Qualify Customer response is highly discouraged and only allowed on an exception basis. A negative risk screen result response is returned as a result of identified risk factors (for example, mishandling of an account, future financial and representational loss to bank).
    • A risk screen override cannot be approved by a branch manager for the following reasons:
      • Existing account currently in collections
      • Account charge off
      • Shared Fraud
      • Hard hold not released
      • Fiduciary (for example, guardian, conservator, custodian, representative payee, personal representative, administrator, trustee, owner, or key executive) on an account (for example, Court Blocked, Estate) does not pass risk screening.
      • A court appointed trustee, owner or key executive on a bankruptcy account does not pass risk screening.
    • A negative risk screen override can be approved by a branch manager, district manager, or above if it meets the following reasons:

Reason for decline

Action

Hard hold for the following reasons on customer related accounts:

  • Loss Prevention Fraud, suspected or fraud victim
  • Bankruptcy Account
  • CIP/CDD error
  • Estate Care
  • Lost/Stolen
  • Identify Theft
  1. Use the Hard Holds and Pledges procedure to verify the hard hold is released.
  2. If the hard hold is released, go back to step 1 and reprocess the risk screening.
    • Positive risk screen result: Go to Step 7: Add authorized signers.
    • Negative risk screen result: Obtain branch manager approval or above to proceed and process the risk screen override. Go to step 3.

Deceased SSN

The account may have been declined due to the SSN reported as belonging to a deceased person by the Social Security Administration.

Note: Bankers are prohibited from removing or altering an owner or key executive to pass risk screening.

  1. Verify the SSN was entered correctly by reviewing the owner’s or key executive’s customer records and reconfirm the information entered with the customer.
  2. SSN was entered:
    • Incorrectly:
      1. Complete the Create or Maintain an Individual Record or Entity Record procedure to correct the SSN.
      2. Go back to step 1 and reprocess the risk screening.
        • Positive risk screen result: Go to the Step 7: Add authorized signers section.
        • Negative risk screen result: Obtain branch manager approval or above to proceed and process the risk screen override. Go to step 3.
    • Correctly: Tell the customer:
      • The account cannot be opened.
      • Account was declined due to information provided by a Consumer Reporting Agency. An Adverse Action Letter will be mailed to individuals who received the decline within 10 business days.

This procedure is complete.

  • A negative risk screen override can be approved by a district manager or above only on an exception basis if there are extenuating circumstances. Go to step 3.

Examples:

  • Decline not related to individual requesting the new account
  • Account closed due to bank error
  • Established banking relationship in good standing
  1. Complete the appropriate action based on the override decision:
    • Override is approved:
      1. Select Management approval obtained for negative risk screen override as the reason for approval from the Approval/Override Reason menu.
      2. Select Continue.
      3. Access Banker Notes and document your branch manager’s or next level of authority name and reason for approval.
      4. Go to the Step 7: Add authorized signers section.
    • Override is not approved: Tell the customer the account cannot be opened. This procedure is complete.

 

Step 7: Add authorized signers

  1. Complete the screen information.
    1. Determine if an existing Certificate of Authority can be cross referenced and used for the new account. To verify existing authorized signers are identical to the individuals on the new account, go to the existing account’s Account Detail screen, select Documents, and review the Certificate of Authority on the Business Account application.
      • Authorized signers are an exact match: Select the applicable option from the Certificate of Authority drop-down menu.
      • Authorized signers are not an exact match: Select Obtain signatures on Business Account Application. Go to step b.

Note: Ensure the individual’s name on the customer record matches the legal name listed on the customer’s primary ID, including middle initials and name suffixes if applicable (for example, Jr., Sr.). Correct the name as needed.

  1. Select Yes or No from the Select Authorized Signers from Business Owners and Key Executives section, Signer? drop-down menu, as applicable, for each owner or key executive.
  2. Complete the Search for Additional Authorized Signers section by searching for additional authorized signers.
  3. Create or update full or limited customer record for each additional authorized signer, if applicable.
  4. Ensure the individual’s name on the customer record matches the legal name listed on their primary ID, including middle initials and suffixes if applicable (for example, Jr., Sr.).
  5. Select Continue.

Notes:

  • Authorized signer for a filed entity can have a limited customer record.
  • If the business is a non-filed entity the authorized signers must have a full customer record and be identified.
  • For a non-filed entity, if authorized signers being added are not present, they cannot be added at this time. Complete the Business Deposit Account: One Individual is Present and One or More Are Not Present procedure for instructions of how to add the authorized signers.
  • The total number of authorized signers you can link to the account’s business relationship is six in this session. You can add more signers later in this procedure.

Example: If the entity and one owner or key executive display in the Additional Relationships section, then you can add only six more individuals to the account’s business relationship as new authorized signers.

  • You cannot add nonindividual owners with or without entity authority and control as an authorized signer.

Step 8: Discuss and select products and services

  1. Discuss the recommended products and services with the customer.

    • Interest-bearing accounts: When verbally discussing rates for deposit products or responding to a customer inquiry while face-to-face (in-person) with a customer, you must provide the correct numerical value of the Annual Percentage Yield (APY) and use the correct full term (Annual Percentage Yield) or acronym (APY). During this discussion, the standard, relationship, or special interest rate may be stated in addition to the Annual Percentage Yield (APY).

Example: You will receive an Annual Percentage Yield (APY) of 0.25% (example only and not actual Yield).

Estate (nonindividual personal representative) and receivership (individual receiver)

 

 

Understand the rules

 

  •       The Customer Identification Program (CIP) requirement is designed to enable the bank to form a reasonable belief about an individual’s and nonindividual’s true identity for all new and existing deposit accounts, loans, financial products, contracts, safe deposit boxes, or any other type of banking service or product.
    •      The process of forming a reasonable belief is taking steps to verify the identity, credentials, identification, and other supporting information provided by potential and existing customers.
    •      You must provide the required disclosures, notices, and information to potential and existing customers.
  •       The Customer Due Diligence (CDD) requirement enables Cayman Bank to know its customers and understand the nature and purpose of accounts and relationships to develop a customer risk profile.
  •       Refer to the CSBB 1FC Program Document for additional details on Sanctions situations, UAR submission, CIP requirements, CDD requirements, and Beneficial Ownership requirements.
  •       Compare the provided customer information to the customer identification (ID) or proof-of-entity documentation.
  •       A completed Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers form must be obtained, certified, and signed by the customer at new account opening or business customer relationship maintenance to be valid and acceptable
    Reference: CIP and CDD Resources
  •       When opening a business deposit account, at least one owner or key executive with entity authority and control must have a TIN (for example, SSN or ITIN). If they do not, the business account cannot be opened.
  •       A customer request to open a new deposit account must not be declined for the:
    •      Account may be open only a short time
    •      Customer has or will have duplicate accounts
  •       Employees may open business deposit accounts for customers meeting the following criteria:
    •      Are nonindividual entity customers (including sole proprietorships, business trusts, business pension or profit-sharing trust, corporations, limited liability companies, limited liability partnerships, joint venture, general partnerships, social and recreational clubs, unincorporated associations, and civic groups).
    •      Have gross annual sales of less than $2 million.
    •      Do not require Treasury Management Services.
    •      Do not have complex lending needs.

If the business does not meet the criteria, the employee must refer the customer to the appropriate partner or affiliate.
Related procedure: Referrals to Partners or Affiliates

  •       Disclosures: If disclosures are not available, the account cannot be opened. A supply of disclosure New Account Kits (NAKs) may be obtained from another location or if the customer wants to receive the disclosure electronically and has access to their email through their mobile device the account can be opened.
  •       Employees must not sign or otherwise place a customer’s signature on a document on the customer’s behalf or in lieu of the customer physically signing. Print or digital copies of signatures obtained from the customer on previous documents must not be used when a signature is required on a new document.
  •       Employees are prohibited from entering into any customer provided agreements, up to and including agreements barring Branch Banking from sharing due diligence information with Financial Crimes Risk Management (FCRM), Internal Audit, regulators, or other similar functions. Any existing accounts with external agreements identified post account opening will be immediately exited.
  •       When opening a new account for a business, the individuals who provide personal financial information in connection with the business must be given the opportunity to elect whether to share personal information with other Cayman Bank affiliates.
  •       Treasury Management deposit products are restricted from being offered to customers (for example, Controlled Disbursement, Stagecoach deposit). Only business account products can be opened by branch employees.
    •      Refer to the Products database for currently available accounts.
    •      Referrals must be referred to the appropriate partner or affiliate.

Related procedure: Referrals to Partners or Affiliates

  •       Employees must not travel outside of the U.S. for purposes of conducting bank business or discussing bank related products or services.
  •       A new account request must be blocked or restricted if the transaction is conducted by, for, or on behalf of countries, entities, or individuals affected by the Foreign Assets Control regulations.
  •       When the tax-responsible customer (for example, business account owner, third party, client, or insolvent party) is an entity, trust, or estate formed in a U.S. territory, a noninterest-earning product must be used.
  •       Prohibited high-risk industries are not permitted to open or maintain deposit accounts or Safe Deposit Box Relationships.
  •       Deposit accounts and Safe Deposit Box Relationships for restricted high-risk industries can be opened after they have been reviewed and approved by Enhanced Due Diligence Center (EDDC).
  •       Certain unregulated or unlicensed financial institutions are prohibited from being opened or maintained. These industries must be reviewed and approved by Enhanced Due Diligence Center (EDDC) prior to opening the account.
  •       If a due diligence review is required, and the customer indicates either of the following, a Suspected Risk Referral (SRR) must be submitted, and a new account request must be denied:
    •      Refuses to provide information required to complete due diligence.
    •      Suspiciously indicates they provided the wrong responses to the compliance questions after the banker already disclosed the enhanced diligence requirements to the customer.
  •       Multiple signature requirements are not allowed on a deposit account.
  •       A fee waiver must not be placed on an account only because the customer has objected to the standard fees.
  •       A Payable on Death (POD) beneficiary may only be added to an account if the entity is a sole proprietorship and is not an IOLTA, RETA, or public fund account. Other types of business entities (for example, corporations, partnerships, or limited liability companies) are ineligible for a POD beneficiary.
  •       First deposit for new account: The minimum deposit requirement must be met and made at the time of the account opening.

Exception: When a court- or government-appointed fiduciary indicates funds are not available to be deposited to the new account but will be deposited in the future, a minimum deposit is not required. Tell the customer the account must be funded within 30 calendar days, or it may be subject to closure.
Examples of court- or government-appointed fiduciary account types are:

  •      Lottery
  •      Attorney client trust
  •      Business trust
  •      Estate – Nonindividual personal representative
  •      Real-estate trust
  •      Representative payee
  •      Individual and nonindividual guardian or conservator
  •      Individual and nonindividual receiverships
  •      Statutory client trust

Note: The minimum deposit amount is always required for a time deposit account.

A nexus (connection) to a sanctioned country
Examples:

An individual with a nexus (connection) to Cuba, Iran, or North Korea

Before opening or maintaining relationships for an account, follow the requirements in the Onboard a customer or other associated party with a nexus to a sanctioned country section in the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Requirements procedure.

  •       All sanctions-related actions should only be performed as directed by FC Risk Management and the Global Sanctions Screening and Reporting Group (GSSRG) team.

The following not all-inclusive list is examples of how to identify a nexus (connection) to Cuba, Iran, or North Korea:

  •      Self-Identify: Conversing with the individual and they provide that information (for example, while completing a transaction request, answering country of citizenship or address questions)
  •      Document Review: Reviewing identification or other documentation the customer provides (for example, Iran Passport, U.S. Passport stating the place of birth is Cuba, proof of address)
  •       If you identify any red flags or unusual activity, submit an SRR.
  •       Open a receivership when a court appoints an individual or entity as receiver to take control of the assets of an insolvent party. The insolvent party may be an individual or nonindividual.

Note: A receiver is typically appointed to control the assets of a single insolvent party. In less common situations, a receiver may be appointed for multiple related insolvent parties.

  •      The court document typically requires the receiver to close the insolvent party’s existing accounts and open a new account titled in the name of the receivership. The receiver may leave funds in the existing accounts to cover outstanding or known items to be paid.
  •      The original or certified copy of the court document appointing a receiver must be obtained and a copy retained for bank records, when the individual acting on behalf of a nonindividual receiver requests to open an account titled in the name of the receivership.
  •       When a new account in the name of the receivership is requested, a business product must be opened even if the insolvent party is an individual.

During this discussion, the standard, relationship, or special interest rate may be stated in addition to the Annual Percentage Yield (APY).

Understand the rules

  •       The Customer Identification Program (CIP) requirement is designed to enable the bank to form a reasonable belief about an individual’s and nonindividual’s true identity for all new and existing deposit accounts, loans, financial products, contracts, safe deposit boxes, or any other type of banking service or product.
    •      The process of forming a reasonable belief is taking steps to verify the identity, credentials, identification, and other supporting information provided by potential and existing customers.
    •      You must provide the required disclosures, notices, and information to potential and existing customers.
  •       The Customer Due Diligence (CDD) requirement enables Cayman Bank to know its customers and understand the nature and purpose of accounts and relationships to develop a customer risk profile.
  •       Refer to the CSBB 1FC Program Document for additional details on Sanctions situations, UAR submission, CIP requirements, CDD requirements, and Beneficial Ownership requirements.
  •       Compare the provided customer information to the customer identification (ID) or proof-of-entity documentation.
  •       A completed Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers form must be obtained, certified, and signed by the customer at new account opening or business customer relationship maintenance to be valid and acceptable
    Reference: CIP and CDD Resources
  •       When opening a business deposit account, at least one owner or key executive with entity authority and control must have a TIN (for example, SSN or ITIN). If they do not, the business account cannot be opened.
  •       A customer request to open a new deposit account must not be declined for the:
    •      Account may be open only a short time.
    •      Customer has or will have duplicate accounts.
  •       Employees may open business deposit accounts for customers meeting the following criteria:
    •      Are nonindividual entity customers (including sole proprietorships, business trusts, business pension or profit-sharing trust, corporations, limited-liability companies, limited-liability partnerships, joint venture, general partnerships, social and recreational clubs, unincorporated associations and civic groups).
    •      Have gross annual sales of less than $2 million.
    •      Do not require Treasury Management Services.
    •      Do not have complex lending needs.

If the business does not meet the criteria, the employee must refer the customer to the appropriate partner or affiliate.

Related procedure: Referrals to Partners or Affiliates

  •       Disclosures: If disclosures are not available, the account cannot be opened. A supply of disclosure New Account Kits (NAKs) may be obtained from another location. If the customer wants to receive the disclosure electronically and has access to their email through their mobile device, the account can be opened.
  •       Employees must not sign or otherwise place a customer’s signature on a document on the customer’s behalf or in lieu of the customer physically signing. Print or digital copies of signatures obtained from the customer on previous documents must not be used when a signature is required on a new document.
  •       Employees are prohibited from entering into any customer provided agreements, up to and including agreements barring Branch Banking from sharing due diligence information with Financial Crimes Risk Management (FCRM), Internal Audit, regulators, or other similar functions. Any existing accounts with external agreements identified after account opening will be immediately exited.
  •       When opening a new account for a business, the individuals who provide personal financial information in connection with the business must be given the opportunity to elect whether to share personal information with other Cayman Bank affiliates.
  •       Treasury Management deposit products are restricted from being offered to customers (for example, Controlled Disbursement, Stagecoach deposit). Only business account products can be opened by branch employees.
    •      Refer to the Products database for currently available accounts.
    •      Referrals must be directed to the appropriate partner or affiliate.

Related procedure: Referrals to Partners or Affiliates

  •       Employees must not travel outside of the U.S. for purposes of conducting bank business or discussing bank related products or services.
  •       A new account request must be blocked or restricted if the transaction is conducted by, for, or on behalf of countries, entities, or individuals affected by the Foreign Assets Control regulations.
  •       When the tax-responsible customer (for example, business account owner, third-party, client, or insolvent party) is an entity, trust, or estate formed in a U.S. territory, a noninterest-earning product must be used.
  •       Prohibited high-risk industries are not permitted to open or maintain deposit accounts or Safe Deposit Box Relationships.
  •       Deposit accounts and Safe Deposit Box Relationships for restricted high-risk industries can be opened after they have been reviewed and approved by Enhanced Due Diligence Center (EDDC).
  •       Certain unregulated or unlicensed financial institutions are prohibited from being opened or maintained. These industries must be reviewed and approved by Enhanced Due Diligence (EDDC) prior to opening the account.
  •       If a due diligence review is required, and the customer indicates either of the following, a Suspected Risk Referral (SRR) must be submitted, and a new account request must be denied:
    •      Refuses to provide information required to complete due diligence.
    •      Suspiciously indicates they provided the wrong responses to the compliance questions after the banker already disclosed the enhanced diligence requirements to the customer.
  •       Multiple signature requirements are not allowed on a deposit account.
  •       A fee waiver must not be placed on an account only because the customer has objected to the standard fees.
  •       A Payable on Death (POD) beneficiary may only be added to an account if the entity is a sole proprietorship, and is not an IOLTA, RETA or public fund account. Other types of business entities (for example, corporations, partnerships, or limited liability companies) are ineligible for a POD beneficiary.
  •       First deposit for new account: The minimum deposit requirement must be met and made at the time of the account opening.

Exception: When a court- or government-appointed fiduciary indicates funds are not available to be deposited to the new account but will be deposited in the future, a minimum deposit is not required. Tell the customer the account must be funded within 30 calendar days, or it may be subject to closure.

Examples of court- or government-appointed fiduciary account types are:

  •      Lottery
  •      Attorney client trust
  •      Business trust
  •      Estate - Nonindividual personal representative
  •      Real-estate trust
  •      Representative payee
  •      Individual and nonindividual guardian or conservator
  •      Individual and nonindividual receiverships
  •      Statutory client trust

Note: The minimum deposit amount is always required for a time deposit account.

  •       A corporation can have a single owner.
  •       Before opening a deposit account, risk screening must be completed on the following individuals:
    •      Owners with 25% or more ownership that have entity authority and control
    •      Key executives with entity authority and control

Note: Owners with less than 25% entity ownership with authority and control added to the business relationship will also be risk screened but it is not required.

Exception: Risk screening is not required for the following individuals:

  •      Nonindividual owners with or without entity authority and control
  •      Individual owners without entity authority and control
  •      Key executives of a U.S. government unit or agency, or Indian tribal government
  •      For benefit of (FBO) accounts for a title company with an approved Title Escrow Service Agreement on file
  •      Trustee of a trust who owns 25% or more of an entity, and authorized signers who are not owners (with entity authority and control)
  •       Girl Scouts USA has established local or regional Girl Scout Councils throughout the U.S. Each council is a nonprofit corporation.
  •       Each Girl Scout council establishes and oversees individual Girl Scout troops, Girl Scout service units, or Girl Scout day camps within its jurisdiction.
  •       Only the Girl Scout council key executive can open Girl Scout troop DBA accounts.
  •       The Girl Scout council’s nonprofit status must be verified.

For additional information, refer to the Business Deposit Account: Entity Verification procedure.

  •       Transaction approvers: Introduce yourself to the customer and explain your role when you are asked to review a transaction or request.

An individual with a nexus (connection) to Cuba, Iran, or North Korea

Before opening or maintaining relationships for an account, follow the requirements in the Onboard a customer or other associated party with a nexus to a sanctioned country section in the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Requirements procedure.

  •       All sanctions-related actions should only be performed as directed by FC Risk Management and the Global Sanctions Screening and Reporting Group (GSSRG) team.

The following not all-inclusive list is examples of how to identify a nexus (connection) to Cuba, Iran, or North Korea:

  •      Self-Identify: Conversing with the individual and they provide that information (for example, while completing a transaction request, answering country of citizenship or address questions)
  •      Document Review: Reviewing identification or other documentation the customer provides (for example, Iran Passport, U.S. Passport stating the place of birth is Cuba, proof of address)
  •       If you identify any red flags or unusual activity, submit an SRR.

Notes:

  • The individual customer records of business owners or key executives with a foreign address must be created in Streamline Business Sales.

  1. Print and ask the customer to complete the Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers (10%) (596622) form.
    Notes:
    • Complete the required banker information in the Bank Use Only section on the Beneficial Owner form.
    • Confirm that all information on the beneficial owners form matches the information on the entity and individual customer records for the business and related parties.
    • When completing the manual beneficial owner form it must either be typed or handwritten but not a combination of both.
    • The Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers form must not contain any alterations, changes, or corrections. If there are any, a new form is required.
    • Do not:
      • Use your Banker Stamp (SRS22 or SRS22M) or any other stamp on the body of the Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers form.
      • Add or write any information on the Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers form including CIP/CDD clearing error instructions or comments outside of the Bank Use Only sections.
  2. Contact the Enhanced Due Diligence Center (EDDC) by email and provide the following information:
    • Subject line: Add type of referral (for example, MSB referral, TPP referral, CBD referral, Crowdfunding referral, Donor Advise Funds referral, or Marketplace [online] Lending referral).
    • Entity’s legal name
    • Enterprise Customer Number (ECN)
    • TIN
    • Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers (10%) (596622) form, and any other business filing or formation documents, or licensing documents obtained
    • High Risk type identified (for example, Internet Gambling, Third-Party Payment Processor, Money Service Business, Cannabis Related Business, Crowdfunding, Donor Advise Funds, Marketplace [online] Lending)
  3. Place documents in a secure branch file until a decision is made on the account, then securely destroy the documents.
  4. Tell the customer they will be notified by the EDDC regarding the final decision to open the business deposit account.

Note: The EDDC will communicate the case’s outcome to the banker and customer. Do not open accounts or products until the EDDC approves.

Tell the customers the account cannot be opened because it was declined due to either or both of the following reasons:

  • No risk screen results display in the Qualify Results field: Select Continue. Go to the Step 6: Add authorized signers section.

Note: Risk screen results may not display if the risk screen response times out. Proceed with the account opening and an approval/override reason will not be required. Day 2 risk screening will still occur.

  • Banker wants to open the account even though the customer is not approved: Overriding a negative Qualify Customer response is highly discouraged and only allowed on an exception basis. A negative risk screen result response is returned for identified risk factors (for example, mishandling of an account, future financial and representational loss to bank).
    • A risk screen override cannot be approved by a branch manager for the following reasons:
      • Existing account currently in collections
      • Account charge off
      • Shared Fraud
      • Hard hold not released
      • Fiduciary (for example, guardian, conservator, custodian, representative payee, personal representative, administrator, trustee, owner, or key executive) on an account (for example, Court Blocked, Estate) does not pass risk screening.
      • A court appointed trustee, owner or key executive on a bankruptcy account does not pass risk screening.
  • A negative risk screen override can be approved by a branch manager, district manager, or above if it meets the following reasons:

Reason for decline

Action

Hard hold for the following reasons on customer related accounts:

  • Loss Prevention Fraud, suspected or fraud victim
  • Bankruptcy Account
  • CIP/CDD error
  • Estate Care
  • Lost/Stolen
  • Identify Theft
  1. Use the Hard Holds and Pledges procedure to verify the hard hold is released.
  2. If the hard hold is released, go back to step 1 and reprocess the risk screening.
    • Positive risk screen result: Go to the Step 6: Add authorized signers section.
    • Negative risk screen result: Obtain branch manager approval or above to proceed and process the risk screen override. Go to step 3.

Deceased SSN

The account may have been declined due to the SSN reported as belonging to a deceased person by the Social Security Administration.

Note: Bankers are prohibited from removing or altering an owner or key executive to pass risk screening.

  1. Verify the SSN was entered correctly by reviewing the owner’s or key executive’s customer records and reconfirm the information entered with the customer.
  2. SSN was entered:
    • Incorrectly:
      1. Complete the Create or Maintain an Individual Record or Entity Record procedure to correct the SSN.
      2. Go back to step 1 and reprocess the risk screening.
        • Positive risk screen result: Go to Step 6: Add authorized signers section.
        • Negative risk screen result: Obtain branch manager approval or above to proceed and process the risk screen override. Go to step 3.
    • Correctly: Tell the customer:
      • The account cannot be opened.
      • Account was declined due to information provided by a Consumer Reporting Agency. An Adverse Action Letter will be mailed to individuals who received the decline within 10 business days.

This procedure is complete.

  • A negative risk screen override can be approved by a district manager or above only on an exception basis if there are extenuating circumstances. Go to step 3.

Examples:

  • Decline not related to individual requesting the new account
  • Account closed due to bank error
  • Established banking relationship in good standing
  1. Complete the appropriate action based on the override decision:

      4. Go to the Step 6: Add authorized signers section.
    • Override is not approved: Tell the customer the account cannot be opened. This procedure is complete.
